### Problem `#223` — Planar Subdivision Enclosure Queries, Tree Exchange & Dense Cut DP (`Luogu P3249` & `CF 1284F / CF 724E`)

#### Part A (`Luogu P3249 — [HNOI2016] 矿区`, [Judge Link](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P3249))

You are given a planar straight-line graph (PSLG) with $N \le 2 \times 10^5$ vertices and $M \le 3N - 6$ undirected segments that partition the plane into bounded polygonal regions (ores) and one unbounded outer face. You must process $Q \le 2 \times 10^5$ online queries. Each query specifies a simple cycle of vertices $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_k$ along the graph edges ($\sum k \le 2 \times 10^5$) that forms the boundary of a mining zone $R$. Output the simplified fraction:

$$\frac{\sum_{f \subset R} (\text{Area}(f))^2}{\sum_{f \subset R} \text{Area}(f)}$$

summed over all bounded elementary faces $f$ enclosed inside the query polygon $R$.

#### Part B (`Codeforces 1284F — New Year and Social Network` & `Codeforces 724E — Goods Transportation`, [Judge Link (CF 1284F)](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1284/F), [Judge Link (CF 724E)](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/724/E))

1. **Tree Cut-Cycle Exchange Bijection (`CF 1284F`)**: Given two trees $T_1, T_2$ on the same $N \le 2.5 \times 10^5$ vertices, construct a sequence of $N - 1$ operations where at step $i$, you remove an edge $e_1 \in E(T_1)$ and replace it with an edge $e_2 \in E(T_2)$ such that the intermediate graph remains a connected tree after every single step!
2. **Dense Prefix-to-Suffix Flow Compression (`CF 724E`)**: $N \le 10^4$ cities sit on a line $1 \dots N$. City $i$ produces $p_i$ goods and can sell at most $s_i$ goods; furthermore, for every pair $1 \le i < j \le N$, up to $c$ goods can be shipped directly from $i$ to $j$. Compute the maximum total goods sold (**Direction B Min-Cut DP**, [Ch 16.1](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)).

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problem #223 — Hint 1 (Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Rejection)"}
- **Part A (`Luogu P3249`)**: A query polygon $C$ on the primal planar graph $G$ is a **primal simple cycle**. By Planar Cycle–Cut Duality ([Ch 15.4](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd)), what is a primal simple cycle $C$ in the planar dual $G^*$? It is a **minimal dual cut** $\delta_{G^*}(S^*)$ separating the enclosed faces $S^*$ from the unbounded outer face $f^*_\infty$!
- **Part B (`CF 1284F` & `CF 724E`)**:
  - In `CF 1284F`, if $e_2 = (u, v)$ is a leaf edge in $T_2$ (say $u$ is a leaf in $T_2$), then in $T_1$, the unique path $P_{T_1}(u, v)$ between $u$ and $v$ is the **fundamental cycle** of $e_2$, and removing $e_2$ from $T_2$ leaves $\{u\}$ as a cut! Which edge $e_1 \in P_{T_1}(u, v)$ not yet replaced can be swapped with $e_2$?
  - In `CF 724E`, see Drill 1.4: running Dinic on $\binom{N}{2} = 5 \times 10^7$ edges will TLE/MLE, whereas converting max-flow to min-cut $x_i \in \{S, T\}$ depends only on the count $k$ of prior vertices in $S$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problem #223 — Hint 2 (Intermediate Algebraic & Structural Model)"}
- **Part A (`Luogu P3249`)**:
  1. Extract all elementary faces of the PSLG using half-edge angle sorting and compute each bounded face's signed area $2 \cdot \text{Area}(f) = \sum_{(u \to v) \in \partial f} (x_u y_v - x_v y_u)$ (faces with negative signed area are the outer unbounded face $f^*_\infty$).
  2. Build the planar dual $G^*$ and take **any spanning tree $T^*$ of $G^*$ rooted at the outer face $f^*_\infty$**, precomputing subtree sums $\text{sub}_1(f^*)$ (sum of $\text{Area}$) and $\text{sub}_2(f^*)$ (sum of $\text{Area}^2$).
  3. When a query cycle $v_1 \to v_2 \to \dots \to v_k \to v_1$ arrives, most dual edges crossing the cycle are non-tree edges in $G^* \setminus T^*$ (which we ignore!). For each cycle edge $(v_i \to v_{i+1})$ whose dual $e^* = (f^*_{\text{left}}, f^*_{\text{right}})$ **is a tree edge in $T^*$**:
     - If $f^*_{\text{left}}$ (the interior of the counterclockwise query polygon) is the **child** of $f^*_{\text{right}}$ in $T^*$, we **add** $\text{sub}(f^*_{\text{left}})$.
     - If $f^*_{\text{right}}$ is the **child** of $f^*_{\text{left}}$ in $T^*$, we **subtract** $\text{sub}(f^*_{\text{right}})$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problem #223 — Full 4-Step Compilation & Solution"}
#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)
- **Part A (`Luogu P3249`)**: Asking for the sum of face weights inside a query cycle $C$ on a planar graph with $\sum |C| \le 2 \times 10^5$ is the canonical signature of **Planar Dual Spanning-Tree Subtree Accumulation** ([Ch 15.4](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd)). Just as a cut in a tree is a single edge, restricting a dual cut $\delta_{G^*}(S^*)$ to a dual spanning tree $T^*$ expresses the indicator vector of any enclosed region $S^*$ as a signed sum of subtree indicators along the boundary $\partial S^* \cap E(T^*)$!
- **Part B (`CF 1284F` & `CF 724E`)**:
  - `CF 1284F` tests the **Graphic Matroid Cut–Cycle Exchange Duality**: peeling $T_2$ leaf-by-leaf from bottom to top, for a leaf $u$ of $T_2$ with parent $v = p_2[u]$, the cut $(\{u\}, V \setminus \{u\})$ in $T_2$ must cross at least one unmerged edge on the $u$-$v$ path in $T_1$; specifically, the **first** unmerged edge on $P_{T_1}(u, v)$ starting from $u$ (found via Link-Cut Tree or DSU + binary lifting) can be safely exchanged with $(u, v)$.
  - `CF 724E` is the foundational benchmark of **Direction B: Max-Flow $\to$ Min-Cut DP** ([Ch 16.1](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)).

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic / Logical Representation
- **Part A (`Luogu P3249`)**: Let $T^*$ be a spanning tree of $G^*$ rooted at $f^*_\infty$. For every face $f^* \neq f^*_\infty$, let $P_{T^*}(f^*_\infty, f^*)$ be the unique root-to-$f^*$ path in $T^*$. For any query region $S^* \subseteq V(G^*) \setminus \{f^*_\infty\}$ bounded by a counterclockwise cycle $C$, walking along $P_{T^*}(f^*_\infty, f^*)$ starts outside $S^*$ ($[f^*_\infty \in S^*] = 0$) and flips between $0$ and $1$ every time it crosses $\partial S^*$:
  $$[f^* \in S^*] = \sum_{e^* = (\text{par}(u^*), u^*) \in P_{T^*}(f^*_\infty, f^*) \cap \partial S^*} \text{sign}(e^*, C)$$
  where $\text{sign}(e^*, C) = +1$ if $u^*$ lies to the **left** (interior) of $C$ and $-1$ if $u^*$ lies to the **right** (exterior) of $C$. Summing over all $f^* \in V(G^*)$ and swapping the order of summation gives:
  $$\sum_{f^* \in S^*} W(f^*) = \sum_{e^* = (\text{par}(u^*), u^*) \in \partial S^* \cap E(T^*)} \text{sign}(e^*, C) \cdot \text{SubtreeSum}_{T^*}(u^*)$$
- **Part B (`CF 724E`)**:
  $$\text{MaxFlow} = \min_{x \in \{0,1\}^N} \left[ \sum_{i=1}^N \left( p_i (1 - x_i) + s_i x_i \right) + \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N} c \cdot x_i (1 - x_j) \right]$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Compilation)
1. **Planar Face Extraction & Dual Tree Prefix Sums (`Luogu P3249`)**:
   - Split each undirected segment into two half-edges $2i$ and $2i+1$. At each vertex $u$, sort outgoing half-edges by polar angle `atan2(dy, dx)`.
   - The next half-edge after $e = (u \to v)$ on the face to the **left** of $e$ is the predecessor of $(v \to u)$ in $v$'s sorted outgoing list.
   - Trace all half-edge cycles; the unique cycle with $\sum (x_u y_v - x_v y_u) < 0$ is $f^*_\infty$.
   - Run DFS on $G^*$ from $f^*_\infty$ to build spanning tree $T^*$, marking which primal half-edges correspond to tree edges in $T^*$ and precomputing $\text{sub}_1[u^*] = \sum (2\text{Area})$ and $\text{sub}_2[u^*] = \sum (2\text{Area})^2$.
   - Answer each query $v_1, \dots, v_k$ in $O(k \log(\text{deg}))$ time by looking up each directed half-edge $(v_i \to v_{i+1})$ and adding/subtracting $\text{sub}[u^*]$ if it is a tree edge of $T^*$.
2. **1D Rolling DP (`CF 724E`)**:
   - Let $dp[k]$ be the minimum cut cost after processing prefix $1 \dots i$, given that $k$ vertices in $1 \dots i$ were placed in $S$ ($x_j = 1$):
     $$dp_{\text{new}}[k] = \min\big( \underbrace{dp[k] + p_i + k \cdot c}_{x_i = 0 \text{ ($i \in T$)}},\; \underbrace{dp[k-1] + s_i}_{x_i = 1 \text{ ($i \in S$)}} \big)$$
   - Runs in $O(N^2)$ time and $O(N)$ memory.

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Broken Gadget Counterexample
- **Toy Trace (`Luogu P3249`)**: Suppose $f^*_1$ (area $4$) and $f^*_2$ (area $6$) are two adjacent unit squares, and the spanning tree $T^*$ is $f^*_\infty \to f^*_1 \to f^*_2$.
  - $\text{sub}_1(f^*_2) = 6$, $\text{sub}_1(f^*_1) = 4 + 6 = 10$.
  - Suppose a query asks for the cycle $C$ enclosing **only** $f^*_1$.
  - As $C$ winds counterclockwise around $f^*_1$:
    - On the outer edge between $f^*_\infty$ and $f^*_1$, $f^*_1$ (the child) is inside $C$, so we add $+\text{sub}_1(f^*_1) = +10$.
    - On the shared edge between $f^*_1$ and $f^*_2$, $f^*_2$ (the child) is **outside** $C$ (to the right of $C$), so we subtract $-\text{sub}_1(f^*_2) = -6$.
  - Net sum: $10 - 6 = 4 = \text{Area}(f^*_1)$!
- **Broken Counterexample (`Luogu P3249`)**: What if a query polygon is given in **clockwise** order instead of counterclockwise? Then every interior face lies to the **right** of the directed cycle edges, negating both the numerator and denominator! Taking the absolute value of the signed sum (or checking the sign of the denominator $\sum \text{Area}(f) > 0$) automatically protects against reversed polygon winding.
::::

### Problem `#224` — Global Minimum Cut on Multigraphs & Degree-Constrained Spanning Trees (`HDU 6081` & `CF 1556H`)

#### Part A (`HDU 6081 — 度度熊的王国战略`, [Judge Link](https://acm.hdu.edu.cn/showproblem.php?pid=6081))

You are given an undirected multigraph $G = (V, E)$ with $N \le 3000$ vertices and $M \le 10^5$ undirected edges with positive integer weights $w_e$. Find the minimum weight of edges whose removal disconnects $G$ into at least two non-empty components (the **Global Minimum Cut** of $G$).

#### Part B (`Codeforces 1556H — DIY Tree`, [Judge Link](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1556/H))

You are given a complete undirected graph $K_N$ on $N \le 50$ vertices with edge weights $w_{uv} \le 100$, and degree upper bounds $d_1, d_2, \dots, d_K$ on the first $K$ vertices ($1 \le K \le \min(N, 5)$). Find the minimum weight of a spanning tree $T$ of $K_N$ such that $\deg_T(i) \le d_i$ for all $1 \le i \le K$. (Contrast when degree-constrained subgraph problems compile to flow/matching vs. when they require Matroid Intersection or Fixed-Parameter Enumeration + Matroid Intersection!)

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problem #224 — Hint 1 (Diagnostic Signal & Decoy Rejection)"}
- **Part A (`HDU 6081`)**: This is a non-planar undirected global minimum cut problem with $N \le 3000, M \le 10^5$.
  - **Observation 1 (Trivial Singleton Cuts)**: For any single vertex $u$, $(\{u\}, V \setminus \{u\})$ is a valid global cut of capacity $\deg_w(u) = \sum_{e \in \delta(u)} w_e$. Thus $\min_{u \in V} \deg_w(u)$ is always an upper bound (and on random/contest testdata, often the exact answer or achievable after contracting heavy edges)!
  - **Observation 2 (Heap-Accelerated Stoer–Wagner, [Ch 16.3](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd))**: Each Maximum Adjacency Search (MAS) phase of Stoer–Wagner runs in $O((N + M) \log N)$ using a priority queue, giving $O(N(N + M)\log N)$ worst-case time (and with Nagamochi–Ibaraki sparse certificates or component checks, runs in milliseconds).
- **Part B (`CF 1556H`)**: Notice that only $K \le 5$ vertices have degree constraints! If $K = 1$, it is trivial. If $K \le 5$, what happens to edges that have **both** endpoints in $\{1, \dots, K\}$ vs. edges that have **at most one** endpoint in $\{1, \dots, K\}$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problem #224 — Hint 2 (Intermediate Algebraic & Structural Model)"}
- **Part A (`HDU 6081`)**: Review the **Stoer–Wagner Maximum Adjacency Search (MAS)** invariant ([Ch 16.3](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)):
  - Build set $A$ starting from any vertex; at each step add $v \notin A$ maximizing $w(A, v) = \sum_{u \in A} w(u, v)$.
  - Let $s$ and $t$ be the second-to-last and last vertices added in the MAS ordering. Then the cut $(\{t\}, V \setminus \{t\})$ of weight $w(V \setminus \{t\}, t)$ is a **minimum $s$-$t$ cut** in the current graph!
  - Record `ans = min(ans, w(V \ {t}, t))`, contract $s$ and $t$ into a single supernode, and repeat $N - 1$ times.
- **Part B (`CF 1556H`)**:
  - There are at most $\binom{K}{2} \le \binom{5}{2} = 10$ edges inside the constrained core $C = \{1, \dots, K\}$. Any acyclic forest $F_0$ inside $C$ can be enumerated in $2^{10} = 1024$ (or even fewer: $6^3 < 250$ labeled forests on $5$ vertices) ways!
  - Once the internal edges $F_0 \subseteq E(C)$ are fixed, every remaining edge $e \in E \setminus E(C)$ is incident to **at most one** vertex in $C$!
  - Therefore, choosing the remaining $N - 1 - |F_0|$ edges to form:
    1. A spanning tree when combined with $F_0$ (**Graphic Matroid $\mathcal{M}_1$**), and
    2. Having at most $d_i - \deg_{F_0}(i)$ edges incident to each $i \in \{1, \dots, K\}$ (**Partition Matroid $\mathcal{M}_2$**)
    is a **Weighted Matroid Intersection** problem ([Ch 21.3](../chapters/ch21-lp-duality-totally-unimodular-matrices-polymatroids.qmd)) on at most $N - 1$ elements (after pre-filtering outside edges to the MST of $V \setminus C$)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problem #224 — Full 4-Step Compilation & Solution"}
#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)
- **Part A (`HDU 6081`)**: Asks for the global minimum cut of an undirected graph with no specified $s, t$. This is the direct domain of **Stoer–Wagner's Algorithm** ([Ch 16.3](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)) and **Nagamochi–Ibaraki Sparse Certificates**.
- **Part B (`CF 1556H`)**: Serves as our **Forward Bridge to Part V ([Ch 21.3](../chapters/ch21-lp-duality-totally-unimodular-matrices-polymatroids.qmd))**. Why can't we solve degree-constrained spanning tree by Bipartite Matching or Max-Flow? Because the **spanning tree (graphic matroid)** constraint $\mathcal{M}_1$ is non-bipartite! However, when we intersect $\mathcal{M}_1$ (Graphic Matroid) with $\mathcal{M}_2$ (Partition Matroid on $\{1, \dots, K\}$), any edge with **two** endpoints in $\{1, \dots, K\}$ would belong to two parts of the partition (turning $\mathcal{M}_2$ into an intersection of two matroids, i.e., 3-Matroid Intersection, which is NP-hard). Because $K \le 5$, enumerating the forest $F_0$ inside $\{1, \dots, K\}$ reduces the remaining problem to clean **2-Matroid Weighted Intersection**!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic / Logical Representation
- **Part A (`Stoer–Wagner Proof Invariant`, [Ch 16.3](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd))**: Let $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n$ be the MAS ordering ($s = v_{n-1}, t = v_n$). Call a vertex $v_i$ **active** with respect to an $s$-$t$ cut $(X, Y)$ if $v_i$ and $v_{i-1}$ lie on **opposite** sides of $(X, Y)$. By induction on active vertices using submodularity of $w(A, \cdot)$, for every active $v_i$:
  $$w(A_{i-1}, v_i) \le w(X \cap (A_{i-1} \cup \{v_i\}),\; Y \cap (A_{i-1} \cup \{v_i\}))$$
  Applying this to the last active vertex $v_n = t$ gives $w(A_{n-1}, t) \le w(X, Y)$ for every $s$-$t$ cut $(X, Y)$!
- **Part B (`CF 1556H`)**:
  1. First, compute the Minimum Spanning Tree $T_{\text{out}}$ of the unconstrained vertices $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ in $O(N^2)$. Any edge inside $\{K+1, \dots, N\}$ not in $T_{\text{out}}$ is never needed, shrinking the candidate edge pool outside $E(C)$ to at most $(N - K - 1) + K(N - K) \le 45 + 225 = 270$ edges!
  2. For each valid forest $F_0 \subseteq E(\{1, \dots, K\})$ obeying $\deg_{F_0}(i) \le d_i$:
     - Find a minimum-weight common independent set $I$ of size $N - 1 - |F_0|$ in $\mathcal{M}_1 / F_0$ (graphic matroid contracted by $F_0$) and $\mathcal{M}_2$ (partition matroid where edge $(i, u)$ with $i \le K < u$ has colour $i$ with capacity $d_i - \deg_{F_0}(i)$, and edges in $T_{\text{out}}$ have colour $0$ with capacity $\infty$).

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Compilation)
1. **Heap-Based Stoer–Wagner (`HDU 6081`)**:
   - First check if the graph is already disconnected ($0$).
   - Maintain adjacency lists with Union-Find / contraction lists. In phase $p = 1 \dots N-1$:
     - Push `(w[v], v)` into a `std::priority_queue` as $w(A, v)$ increases.
     - Let $s, t$ be the last two popped vertices; update `ans = min(ans, w[t])`.
     - Merge $t$'s adjacency list into $s$ (combining parallel edges to the same neighbor).
2. **Weighted Matroid Intersection (`CF 1556H`)**:
   - In each augmentation step from current independent set $I$, build the exchange digraph on the $m \le 270$ candidate edges:
     - Source set $X_1 = \{e \notin I : I \cup \{e\} \in \mathcal{M}_1\}$, Sink set $X_2 = \{e \notin I : I \cup \{e\} \in \mathcal{M}_2\}$.
     - For $y \in I, x \notin I$: add $y \to x$ if $I \setminus \{y\} \cup \{x\} \in \mathcal{M}_1$; add $x \to y$ if $I \setminus \{y\} \cup \{x\} \in \mathcal{M}_2$.
     - Find the shortest (min-weight, then min-hops) path from $X_1$ to $X_2$ via SPFA/Bellman-Ford and take the symmetric difference $I \gets I \triangle P$.

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Broken Gadget Counterexample
- **Toy Trace (`Stoer–Wagner`, $N = 4$)**: Two triangles $(1,2,3)$ and $(2,3,4)$ with heavy triangle edges $10$ and a single bridge-like pair $(1,2)=10, (2,3)=10, (1,3)=10$ vs. $(3,4)=2, (2,4)=3$:
  - Start MAS at $1$: $A_1 = \{1\}$. Weights to $A_1$: $w(2)=10, w(3)=10, w(4)=0$.
  - Add $2$: $A_2 = \{1, 2\}$. Weights to $A_2$: $w(3) = 10+10 = 20, w(4) = 3$.
  - Add $3$: $A_3 = \{1, 2, 3\}$. Weight to $A_3$: $w(4) = 3 + 2 = 5$.
  - Last two vertices: $s = 3, t = 4$, cut of $t = 4$ is $w(A_3, 4) = 5$. Contract $3$ and $4$ into supernode $\{3,4\}$, and subsequent phases find cuts of size $\ge 20$. Global min-cut is $5$.
- **Broken Counterexample (`CF 1556H`)**: What if you do **not** enumerate the internal edges $F_0$ inside $\{1, \dots, K\}$ and instead put all $\binom{N}{2}$ edges directly into the matroid intersection algorithm? An edge $(1, 2)$ between two constrained vertices consumes degree quota at **both** vertex $1$ and vertex $2$. The family of edge sets obeying degree bounds at all vertices simultaneously is a **2-matching / b-matching** constraint (itself an intersection of two partition matroids if bipartite, or non-matroidal in general), so intersecting it with the Graphic Matroid $\mathcal{M}_1$ breaks the 2-matroid exchange property and causes shortest augmenting paths to produce invalid degrees!
::::

### 3.2 Failure Mode Self-Audit (`FM-14` through `FM-16`)

Before moving on, verify that you can answer each of the following three structural audit questions from memory.

#### Audit 1 — `FM-14`: Goldberg's Unshifted Negative Capacity & The Trivial $S = \emptyset$ Cut Trap ([Ch 14.2](../chapters/ch14-fractional-programming-maximum-density-subgraphs.qmd))

> **Self-Audit Question**: In Goldberg's Maximum Density Subgraph network for maximizing $\frac{|E(S)|}{|S|}$, why do we add a large shift constant $U \ge \Delta(G)$ to every source edge $c(s, u) = U$ and sink edge $c(u, t) = U + 2\lambda - \deg_G(u)$, and how do you guarantee that the residual $s$-side set $S$ is non-empty ($S \neq \emptyset$)?

:::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="FM-14 Self-Audit Verification"}
1. **Why $U \ge \Delta(G)$ is Mandatory**: Without $U$, the sink capacity $2\lambda - \deg_G(u)$ is negative whenever $\deg_G(u) > 2\lambda$, which invalidates Dinic's non-negative capacity invariant. Adding $U$ to both $c(s, u)$ and $c(u, t)$ adds exactly $U$ to every vertex $u$'s contribution regardless of whether $u \in S$ (cuts $u \to t$) or $u \in \bar{S}$ (cuts $s \to u$), shifting every cut capacity by the constant $+U \cdot |V|$ without changing the relative ordering of subsets $S \subseteq V$.
2. **Preventing the Trivial $S = \emptyset$ Cut**: Because $S = \emptyset$ always yields cut capacity $U \cdot |V| + 2(\lambda \cdot 0 - 0) = U \cdot |V|$, any $\lambda > \lambda^*$ has $S = \emptyset$ as the unique minimum cut. During binary search, test strict feasibility `max_flow < U * N` (with $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{N(N-1)}$ spacing between distinct rational densities $\frac{E_1}{V_1} \neq \frac{E_2}{V_2}$), and reconstruct the subgraph at the last strictly feasible $\lambda_{\text{low}} < \lambda^*$ where $S_{\min} = \{u \in V : s \rightsquigarrow_{G_f} u\}$ is guaranteed to be non-empty!
::::

#### Audit 2 — `FM-15`: Directed Planar Dual Orientation & Boundary Short-Circuiting ([Ch 15.2–15.3](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd))

> **Self-Audit Question**: When converting a directed planar $s$-$t$ cut network into a dual shortest-path problem from $s^*$ to $t^*$, how do you verify in $30$ seconds on scratch paper that your $90^\circ$ rotation direction is not backwards, and why must outer-boundary edges incident to $s^*$ and $t^*$ be strictly one-way (or carefully directed)?

:::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="FM-15 Self-Audit Verification"}
1. **The $1 \times 1$ Corner Cut Sanity Check**: Always draw the $1$-vertex source cut $S = \{s\}$ at the corner $s = (0,0)$. The only primal edges in $\delta^+(S)$ are the two outgoing edges from $(0,0)$: $(0,0) \to (0,1)$ and $(0,0) \to (1,0)$. Check that your dual graph routes $s^* \to f_{(1,1)} \to t^*$ using the weights of **those two outgoing edges** from $(0,0)$, not the incoming edges $(0,1) \to (0,0)$ and $(1,0) \to (0,0)$!
2. **No Free Boundary Teleportation**: Never connect internal faces to $s^*$ with zero-weight reverse edges or allow a path to enter $s^*$ and exit $s^*$ at another boundary face. In a multi-terminal boundary problem (`CSP-S 2021 交通规划`, [Ch 15.3](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd)), the outer boundary segments between adjacent same-colored terminals are **blocked** (or simply omitted as dual terminals); only the $2r$ boundary intervals where terminal colors switch $0 \leftrightarrow 1$ become active dual terminals $v^*_1, \dots, v^*_{2r}$.
::::

#### Audit 3 — `FM-16`: Gomory–Hu Undirected Precondition & Supernode Contraction ([Ch 16.4](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd))

> **Self-Audit Question**: Why does a Gomory–Hu cut tree fail to exist on directed graphs, and why is **Gusfield's algorithm** preferred over classical Gomory–Hu contraction in competitive programming implementations?

:::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="FM-16 Self-Audit Verification"}
1. **Undirected Symmetry Requirement**: On a directed cycle $1 \xrightarrow{1} 2 \xrightarrow{1} 3 \xrightarrow{1} 1$, $\text{mincut}(u, v) = 1$ for every ordered pair, yet any tree on 3 vertices has a leaf whose single incident edge must represent both $\text{mincut}(u, v)$ and $\text{mincut}(v, u)$ simultaneously — impossible when $\text{mincut}(u, v) \neq \text{mincut}(v, u)$! Furthermore, uncrossing of minimum cuts requires symmetric submodularity $f(A) = f(V \setminus A)$.
2. **Why Gusfield Beats Manual Supernode Contraction**: Classical Gomory–Hu requires contracting the connected components of $T \setminus \{V_i\}$ into supernodes before each max-flow call (and failing to contract — e.g., running max-flow only on the induced subgraph of $V_i$ — produces wrong cuts because paths can detour through $V \setminus V_i$). Gusfield's algorithm runs all $N - 1$ Dinic calls on the **original, unmodified graph $G$**, updating only the $N$-element parent array `if (vis[u] && p[u] == t) p[u] = s` in 8 lines of bug-free code.
::::

## Section 4: Readiness Bridge to Part V (`Ch 17`–`Ch 21`: Min-Cost Max-Flow, Equation Differencing & LP Duality)

### 4.1 Part IV Cut-Linearization & Structural Compression Cheat Sheet

| Target Objective / Query | Algebraic Linearization / Dual Transformation | Compiled Solver & Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **0-1 Fractional Ratio** $\max \frac{\sum a_i x_i}{\sum b_i x_i}$ | $F(\lambda) = \max_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{F}} \sum (a_i - \lambda b_i) x_i \ge 0$ | Dinkelbach Newton step $\lambda_{k+1} = \frac{f(\mathbf{x}^*)}{g(\mathbf{x}^*)}$ or Binary Search ([Ch 14.1](../chapters/ch14-fractional-programming-maximum-density-subgraphs.qmd)) |
| **Maximum Density Subgraph** $\max_{\emptyset \neq S \subseteq V} \frac{\|E(S)\|}{\|S\|}$ | $\min_{S \subseteq V} \big[ U\|V\| + \sum_{u \in S}(U + 2\lambda - \deg(u)) + \sum_{\bar{S}} U + \|\delta(S)\| \big]$ | Goldberg Shifted Network: $c(s,u)=U$, $c(u,v)=1$, $c(u,t)=U+2\lambda-\deg(u)$ ([Ch 14.2](../chapters/ch14-fractional-programming-maximum-density-subgraphs.qmd)) |
| **Bottleneck Degree Ratio** $\max_{\emptyset \neq S} \min_{u \in S} \frac{\deg_S(u)}{\deg_G(u)}$ | Monotone $k$-core implication $u \in S \implies \deg_S(u) \ge \lambda \deg_G(u)$ | Greedy Priority-Queue Peeling of argmin $\frac{\deg_S(u)}{\deg_G(u)}$ in $O((N+M)\log N)$ ([Ch 14.3](../chapters/ch14-fractional-programming-maximum-density-subgraphs.qmd)) |
| **Planar $s$-$t$ Min-Cut** ($s, t$ on outer face) | Split outer face into $s^*$ (left of $s \to t$) and $t^*$ (right of $s \to t$); right-hand $90^\circ$ rotation for directed edges | Single Dijkstra pass on $G^*$ in $O(F \log F)$ ([Ch 15.1–15.2](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd)) |
| **Planar $2k$-Boundary Bicolorable Cut** | $2r$ color-alternating boundary transitions $v^*_1, \dots, v^*_{2r}$ around outer face | $2r$ Dijkstra runs + Non-Crossing Catalan Interval DP in $O(r F \log F + r^3)$ ([Ch 15.3](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd)) |
| **Planar Polygon Enclosure Sum** $\sum_{f \subset R} W(f)$ | Dual Spanning Tree $T^*$ rooted at $f^*_\infty$; signed subtree sum across $\partial R \cap E(T^*)$ | Half-Edge Face Extraction + $O(\|\partial R\| \log d)$ Tree Lookup ([Ch 15.4](../chapters/ch15-planar-cycle-cut-duality-shortest-paths.qmd)) |
| **Direction B Dynamic Line/Tree Cut** ($N, Q \le 2 \times 10^5$) | $M_i = \begin{pmatrix} p_i & p_i \\ s_i + c_{i-1} & s_i \end{pmatrix}$ in $(+, \min)$ semiring | Dynamic DP / Tropical Segment Tree in $O(Q \log N)$ ([Ch 16.1](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)) |
| **Undirected Global Min-Cut** ($\min_{\emptyset \neq S \subsetneq V} \|\delta(S)\|$) | Maximum Adjacency Search (MAS): last two vertices $s = v_{n-1}, t = v_n$ satisfy $\lambda(s,t) = w(V \setminus \{t\}, t)$ | Stoer–Wagner Contraction in $O(NM + N^2 \log N)$ ([Ch 16.3](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)) |
| **All-Pairs Undirected Min-Cuts** ($\binom{N}{2}$ pairs) | Uncrossing submodular cuts form an ultrametric bottleneck tree $\lambda_G(u,v) = \min_{e \in P_T(u,v)} w_e$ | Gusfield's $N-1$ Max-Flows on unmodified $G$ ([Ch 16.4](../chapters/ch16-mincut-dp-global-mincut-gomory-hu-trees.qmd)) |

### 4.2 What Changes in Part V? (From Feasibility & Cut Capacity to Cost-Driven Optimization)

Across Parts I through IV, every flow edge had only a **capacity** $c(e)$ (plus an optional lower bound $l(e)$). If we wanted to optimize a linear objective over subsets or assignments, we had to encode all costs into **cut capacities** ($s$-$t$ minimum cuts) or **binary search on a threshold** ($\lambda$).

In **Part V ([Ch 17](../chapters/ch17-mcmf-foundations-potentials-slope-negative-cycles.qmd)–[Ch 21](../chapters/ch21-lp-duality-totally-unimodular-matrices-polymatroids.qmd))**, every edge $e = (u \to v)$ gains an independent **unit cost $w(e)$** alongside its capacity $[l(e), u(e)]$, unlocking five transformative modelling paradigms:

1. **Primal-Dual Potentials, Slope Convexity & Negative Cycles ([Ch 17](../chapters/ch17-mcmf-foundations-potentials-slope-negative-cycles.qmd))**: Why the minimum-cost flow function $C(f)$ is piecewise-linear and **convex** in the flow volume $f$ (connecting directly to WQS binary search / Alien's Trick in Part VI!), how Johnson potentials $\pi_u$ maintain non-negative reduced costs $w^\pi(u \to v) = w(u \to v) + \pi_u - \pi_v \ge 0$, and how lower bounds with costs compile into mandatory negative-cycle eliminations (`UVa 10806`, `UOJ #455`).
2. **Convex Marginal Edge Splitting & Degree Penalties ([Ch 18](../chapters/ch18-convex-marginal-splitting-degree-penalties-tournaments.qmd))**: Compiling separable convex costs $\Phi(f_e)$ into parallel unit-capacity edges with non-decreasing marginal differences $\Delta_k = \Phi(k) - \Phi(k-1)$, and modeling tournament triplets $\binom{\text{deg}^+(u)}{2}$ in Landau's theorem (`Luogu P4249 剪刀石头布`, `WC2007`).
3. **The Equation Differencing Method ($\Delta E_t = E_t - E_{t-1}$, [Ch 19](../chapters/ch19-k-interval-coverage-equation-difference-method.qmd))**: Compiling linear systems of range inequalities $L_t \le \sum_{i \in I_t} x_i \le R_t$ into exact flow conservation at vertices by taking consecutive row differences — turning interval coverage and employee scheduling problems (`NOI2008 志愿者招募`, `CF 802C`) into mechanical network compilations without guesswork.
4. **Vertex-Disjoint Cycle Covers, Dynamic Server Activation & Hub Graphs ([Ch 20](../chapters/ch20-cycle-covers-dynamic-scheduling-resource-reuse-hubs.qmd))**: Modeling multi-vehicle routing, napkin/surgical-instrument sterilization delays (`餐巾计划问题`), and lazy waiting-multiplier queues (`NOI2012 美食节`).
5. **LP Duality, Total Unimodularity & Polymatroid Intersection ([Ch 21](../chapters/ch21-lp-duality-totally-unimodular-matrices-polymatroids.qmd))**: Proving *why* all our flow and cut networks produce integer optima via Totally Unimodular (TU) constraint matrices, dualizing unfamiliar primal LPs into flow networks (`ZJOI2013 防守战线`), and extending beyond flow to Matroid & Polymatroid Intersection (as previewed in Problem `#224B`).

If you scored **18 / 24 or higher** on Checkpoint IV and passed all three `FM-14`–`FM-16` self-audits, you are ready to enter **[Chapter 17 — Min-Cost Max-Flow Foundations: Potentials, Convexity of the Cost Curve & Negative Cycles](../chapters/ch17-mcmf-foundations-potentials-slope-negative-cycles.qmd)**.
